extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR applicants and recipients (small business concerns), Grants Management Officials, NIH awarding components, hospital finance administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and mandatory certifications, reporting, approvals, monitoring, and cost principles that SBIR/STTR small business recipients (and associated hospitals) must follow during award lifecycle, plus NIH rules for research patient care costs under grants. Focuses on life cycle certifications, foreign disclosures, subaward prior approvals, repayment authority, RPPRs, Phase II reporting, and hospital patient care cost rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBC–Research institution intellectual property agreement certification
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the face page of the grant application, the SBC’s AOR certifies that the agreement with the research institution is satisfactory to the SBC and will be effective at the time the grant award is made. Prior to award a copy of the agreement must be furnished to the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification covers the parties' intellectual property rights and rights, if any, to carry out follow-on research, development, or commercialization of the subject research.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR inventions and patents statutory coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR recipients are covered by 35 U.S.C. 200-212 and 37 CFR Part 401 with respect to inventions and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Grants to For-Profit Organizations—Administrative Requirements—Intellectual Property for applicable requirements and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR data sharing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR applicants must comply with NIH DMS policy as modified by the Small Business Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final data would not be amenable to sharing (e.g., proprietary data), the SBC should explain that in the application. NIH will not release data outside the Federal government without the recipient’s permission for 20 years from completion of the project, whether or not the award meets NIH data-sharing thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life Cycle Certification requirement (SBIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All SBIR Phase I and Phase II recipients must complete a Life Cycle Certification at all times set forth in the Notice of Award; certification includes checking all boxes and an authorized officer signing and dating each time required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required times: Phase I—at time of receiving final payment or disbursement; Phase II—prior to receiving >50% of total award and prior to final payment. Certifications must be submitted within I-RPPR and F-RPPR (Section G.1) via eRA Commons no later than 120 calendar days from period of performance end date. I-RPPR/F-RPPR will be rejected unless all completed Life Cycle Certifications are received. Failure may result in corrective actions, withholding, suspension, or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life Cycle Certification does not replace Funding Agreement Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Life Cycle Certification requirements do not impact the SBIR Funding Agreement Certification required by all SBIR applicants for new or renewal grants, which is required prior to award of a new award or competing renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure they complete both as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification indicates compliance by drawing/requesting funds
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR recipients indicate compliance with Life Cycle Certification requirements by drawing or requesting funds from the Payment Management System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipient cannot complete the certification or ensure compliance with the process, they must notify the GMO immediately; unresolved issues may lead to voiding or termination of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification legal consequences and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal government relies on certification information to ensure compliance. If the Grants Management Officer believes the business is not meeting funding agreement requirements, the agency may request clarification and documentation. False or incomplete information can lead to criminal, civil, or administrative remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each person signing a certification may be prosecuted for providing false information; government remedies listed include fines, treble damages under False Claims Act, Program Fraud penalties, civil recovery, suspension/debarment, and termination of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator time commitment (SBIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal investigator spent more than half of their time (based on a 40-hour work week) as an employee of the recipient or has requested and received a written deviation from this requirement from the Grants Management Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a deviation is approved by NIH, the certification will document the adjusted percentage of time approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior/subsequent funding and 'essentially equivalent work' disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: All, essentially equivalent work, or a portion of the work performed under this project: (a) has not been submitted for funding to NIH or another Federal agency; (b) has been submitted but not funded under any other grant, contract, subcontract, or other transaction; (c) a portion has been funded by another grant/contract/subcontract as described in the proposal and approved in writing by the Grants Management Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must accurately report previous submissions/funding and obtain written approvals when portions are funded elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance percentage obligations (SBIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the award the recipient will have performed the applicable percentage of work unless a deviation is approved in writing by the Grants Management Officer. Options include: SBIR Phase I—at least two-thirds (66 2/3%) of the research; SBIR Phase II—at least half (50%) of the research; or percent deviation approved in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification options reflect expected SBIR share of performance; failure to meet these without approved deviation may have consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work location and staffing expectations (SBIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The research/research and development is performed in the United States unless a deviation is approved in writing by the Grants Management Officer; performed at recipient's facilities with the recipient's employees, except as otherwise indicated in the SBIR application and approved in the Notice of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must notify the Federal agency if all or a portion of the authorized work is subsequently funded by another Federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifier authority and truthfulness attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: The individual certifying on behalf of the recipient will certify they are: (1) an officer of the business concern authorized to represent it and sign the certification; (2) representing that information provided in the certification and application is true and correct as of the date of submission; (3) acknowledging that intentional or negligent misrepresentation may result in criminal, civil, or administrative sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific statutory penalties and enforcement authorities to which the signer is subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life Cycle Certification requirement (STTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All STTR Phase I and Phase II recipients must complete a Life Cycle Certification at all times set forth in the Notice of Award; includes checking all boxes and an authorized officer signing and dating each time required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required times: Phase I—at final payment/disbursement; Phase II—prior to receiving >50% and prior to final payment. STTR recipients must submit certifications in I-RPPR and F-RPPR via eRA Commons no later than 120 calendar days from period end. Failure may lead to corrective actions, withholding, suspension, or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator time commitment (STTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal investigator spent more than half of their time as an employee of the recipient or the research institution, or the recipient has requested and received a written deviation from this requirement from the Grants Management Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a deviation is approved by NIH, the certification will document the adjusted percentage of time approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR performance percentage obligations and management control
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the award it will have performed the applicable percentage of work unless a deviation approved in writing by the Grants Management Officer: STTR Phase I—at least forty (40%) of the research; STTR Phase II—at least forty (40%) of the research. Additionally, the small business concern, and not the single partnering Research Institution, is exercising management direction and control of the performance of the STTR funding agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification options include completed work percentages and N/A if work not completed. Management/control requirement is explicit for STTR awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval requirement for adding new subawards
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR recipients are required to seek prior approval when adding a new subaward to a project post-award where the arrangement was not originally part of the peer-reviewed and approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All prior approval requests must be submitted through the eRA Commons Prior Approval Module per NIHGPS section 8.1.3. The recipient must either submit an updated SBIR STTR Foreign Disclosure Form or state that there are no updates. A foreign risk assessment is required for the entity selected for the subaward; the recipient must receive official written approval from the NIH Grants Management Official prior to signing a subaward agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repayment and recovery authority for material misstatements or ownership changes
rubrics_metrics.description: An SBC will be required to repay all amounts received from NIH under the award if: (1) the SBC makes a material misstatement that NIH determines poses a risk to national security; or (2) there is a change in ownership, change in entity structure, or other substantial change in circumstances of the SBC that NIH determines poses a risk to national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repayment procedures provided in NIHGPS Section 8.5.4 apply; additional noncompliance remedies in NIHGPS Section 8.5.2 may apply. Follow Guidance for Repayment of Grant Funds to the NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on foreign subawards and approved mechanism for international collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH no longer recognizes foreign subawards. All international research collaborations must use the collaborative international research award mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients contemplating international arrangements should consult the GMO early and use the appropriate NIH mechanism rather than foreign subawards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and update obligations for relationships with foreign countries of concern (post-award)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR recipients are responsible for monitoring relationships with foreign countries of concern post-award and must submit an updated disclosure form to report: any change to a disclosure; any material misstatement posing a national security risk; any change of ownership/entity structure or other substantive change NIH determines poses a national security risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular annual updates are required at all RPPR submissions. For changes occurring between RPPRs, updated disclosures are required within 30 days of changes in ownership, entity structure, covered individual, or other substantive changes. Upload updated disclosures using the Foreign Disclosure Request for Additional Materials (RAM) feature in eRA Commons. NIH may terminate awards for material failures to comply if relationships meet risk criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I Final RPPR timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Phase I recipient does not intend to submit a Phase II application within four months of the Phase I project period end date, then Phase I Final RPPR must be submitted to the Grants Management Office of the Awarding Component within 120 days of the completion date of the Phase I grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application for a Phase II or Phase IIB is submitted before the final report for Phase I would otherwise be due, an Interim-RPPR is required; if the Type 2/Phase II application is funded NIH will treat the Interim-RPPR as the annual performance report for the final year of the previous competitive segment; if not funded, the Interim-RPPR will be treated as the Final-RPPR. Final RPPR instructions are on NIH's website (Chapter 7.3, SBIR/STTR RPPRs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II data collection requirement for SBIR.gov reporting database
rubrics_metrics.description: Each small business concern applying for a Phase II award is required to update the appropriate information in the reporting database on SBIR.gov for any of its prior Phase II awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apportionment of sales or additional investment across multiple Phase II awards is allowed if apportionment is noted. Update upon completion of the last deliverable (Final RPPR, Federal Financial Report, Final Invention Statement) and voluntarily annually thereafter for at least 5 years. Data entered is privileged and confidential (15 U.S.C. 638(k)(4)) and not subject to FOIA; viewable only by authorized Government Officials under NDA. Examples of data: revenue from sale of new products/services resulting from Phase II research; additional investment from any source other than Phase I/II awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for negotiating research patient care rate (hospital recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any hospital that, as a direct recipient of NIH funds, expects to incur more than $100,000 in patient care costs in any single budget period on a single NIH grant must either have in place or take steps to negotiate a research patient care rate agreement with the cognizant CAS office. These rates must be shown in all requests and/or claims for reimbursement of research patient care costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals that expect to incur $100,000 or less per budget period (and patient care for consortium participants/contractors) are subject to Special Procedures for Certain Hospitals. Failure to negotiate a research patient care rate with CAS when required may result in disallowance of all research patient care costs charged to a grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable research patient care costs principle
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patient is receiving service or care that neither differs from usual patient care nor results in expenses greater than those that would have been incurred if the study had not existed, then the grant will generally not support the costs. When the research extends hospitalization or imposes procedures/tests/services beyond usual care, the grant may pay the additional costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must decide whether hospitalization period/tests/services have been extended beyond usual care and document exceptions. NIH funds may pay all costs for individuals who would not have been hospitalized or received such tests/services except for their participation in research (examples: healthy volunteers, certain controls, economically unable patients, etc.). Investigator has responsibility in deciding to include patients with full charges to the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for computing research patient care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research patient care costs, whether expressed as a rate or an amount, shall be computed consistent with principles and procedures used by the Medicare program for determining reasonable-cost-based Medicare reimbursement. Separate cost centers must be established for each discrete bed unit for allocating routine costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When provisional rates are used as basis for award, the amount awarded is the maximum NIH will reimburse; provisional rates must be adjusted if a lower final rate is negotiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost treatment for research patient care activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs should not be paid on any cost component representing the cost of research patient care activities. Research patient care rates include indirect costs related to 'hospital-type' employees supported as direct costs under a grant, so salaries/wages of hospital-type employees must be excluded from the salary and wage base used to claim indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related fringe benefits should also be excluded if part of the S&W base. If a total-direct-costs base is used, hospital-type salaries and any other base costs chargeable via a research patient care rate must be excluded. If a grant provides funding exclusively for research patient care activities, no separate indirect costs normally allowed. Foreign organizations must exclude all indirect expenses from charges to the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for hospitals without negotiated rates (recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not meet the threshold but has a currently negotiated research patient care rate, that rate will be used regardless of expected amount. In other cases, the recipient will be reimbursed at a rate not to exceed the lesser of actual research patient care costs or the rate included in its Medicare cost report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to direct recipients; separate rules apply for consortium participants/contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for consortium participant hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hospital incurring research patient care costs is not the recipient, the recipient is responsible for establishing the reimbursable rate unless the hospital is a direct HHS award recipient with a negotiated research patient care rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a participating hospital expects to incur >$100,000, the recipient must negotiate a rate for that hospital unless the relationship is 'less-than-arms-length'—contact GMO to determine if CAS should negotiate. If a participating hospital expects $100,000 or less, the recipient will use the lesser of actual costs or the rate in the hospital’s Medicare cost report. Thresholds apply to each hospital individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial responsibilities and third-party recoveries for patient care
rubrics_metrics.description: If patient care costs are funded by the grant, amounts recovered from third parties must be credited to the grant. Patient charges must be adjusted to cost before applying third-party recoveries; the remaining balance of allowable costs may then be charged to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient obligated to pursue third-party recovery and document efforts. Example formula provided: Standard Fee Schedule x Negotiated Rate = Cost—Insurance = Maximum Charge to NIH Grant (illustrative numbers given). Funds recovered from third parties for tests developed for research and subsequently billed must be credited to the grant account.
